exposure: Type of cervical ripening agent (osmotic dilator vs. prostaglandins)
outcome: Time between administration of the agent and onset of labor
Time from onset of labor to delivery
cohort: 82 women undergoing trial of labor after cesarean (TOLAC) requiring cervical ripening agents
finding: This pilot study found that the use of an osmotic dilator for cervical ripening in women undergoing TOLAC is a viable option, with similar maternal and neonatal outcomes compared to prostaglandins.
mod_finding: Vaginal birth rate (including operative delivery) was 55% in the osmotic dilator group vs. 51% in the dinoprostone group (P 0.886).
